records.real_world_identity_notes: The 1998 long-tail Nissan R390 GT1. NISMO records the long-tail aerodynamic revision and Nissan-built sequential transmission for 1998; RSS describes its fictionalized Nisumo R39 with the same 1997-98 lineage, primarily-1998 long-tail form, and 3,495 cc twin-turbo V8.
records.confidence_basis: RSS's first-party pack documentation and installed metadata identify the exact fingerprinted implementation as the primarily-1998 long-tail, 3,495 cc twin-turbo V8 car. NISMO independently gives that same combination only to the 1998 R390 GT1 and records its sequential transmission. Six sequential-stick gears, clutch-required move-off, automatic cut/blip, and cockpit wheel equipment were directly observed.
records.identity_basis: RSS Classic Endurance Pack 1 readme, PDF/printed page 3, says the Nisumo R39 was built for 1997 and 1998, depicts the long-tail used primarily in 1998, and uses a 3,495 cc twin-turbo V8. NISMO's own history says the 1998 Nissan R390 GT1 became a long-tail and changed to a Nissan-built sequential transmission. The year, body revision, displacement, engine layout, aspiration, category and fictionalized model token converge on the existing 1998 R390 GT1 record rather than a neighboring Nissan prototype.
records.specification_basis: The existing record retains the real six-speed sequential-stick specification. NISMO independently strengthens sequential construction for the 1998 car, while the fingerprinted RSS v2 drive directly selected six gears through a sequential stick. The mod's automatic downshift blip and D-shaped unlit wheel are implementation behavior and do not rewrite the real-car controls.

records.confidence_notes: The exact Race Sim Studio v2 data.acd was fingerprinted. Six sequential-stick gears, clutch-required move-off, full-throttle and coast-shift acceptance, automatic cut and blip, and a closed D-shaped rim without display or shift lights were observed. Running clutch acceptance remains medium confidence because SimHub's clutch channel recorded activity during the accepted shift and may include car-side intervention.
control_notes: This drive maps Race Sim Studio's fictionalized Nisumo R39 name onto the existing 1998 Nissan R390 GT1 only after first-party specification comparison.
RSS automatically blips the tested downshift. AMS2 and the curated real-car guidance leave that rev matching to the driver.
The RSS cockpit uses a D-shaped rim without wheel-mounted shift lights; those implementation details are kept as AC overrides rather than replacing the curated round, lit rim.
